opportunities.title: Cambridge Africa Climate Collaborative Research Fund 2026/27 (Mastercard Foundation - University of Cambridge Climate Resilience and Sustainability Research Fund, round 3)
opportunities.funder: Mastercard Foundation (administered by University of Cambridge / Cambridge-Africa)
opportunities.program: Africa Climate Collaborative - Cambridge Africa Climate Collaborative Research Fund
opportunities.deadline_text: The deadline for submission is 15th January 2027 and applications can be submitted at any time before this. Timeline: 15th October 2026 Applications open; 15th January 2027 Applications close.
opportunities.funding_text: Research Catalyst Grant for up to GBP 25,000, a Research Project Grant for up to GBP 80,000 or a Workshop Grant for up to GBP 50,000. We do not cover salaries of either investigator, institutional overheads, indirect costs or grant administration costs.
opportunities.duration: Approx. 12 months (Catalyst and Workshop grants) or up to 18 months (Research Project Grant); recommended start not earlier than 1 June 2027
opportunities.eligible_applicants: Pairs of researchers (post-doctoral level or above): one from the University of Cambridge (lead applicant, administers the award) and one from a university or research institution of comparable standing on the African continent. Both must be formally employed at their institutions.
opportunities.eligible_countries: African partner: any country on the African continent; lead must be University of Cambridge
opportunities.cgiar_eligibility_notes: Cannot lead (Cambridge applicant is always lead). The Alliance could act as the Africa-based partner only through an Alliance researcher formally employed and based at an Alliance office in Africa (e.g., Nairobi), and only if the panel accepts the Alliance as a 'research institution of comparable standing to a university' on the African continent - not stated explicitly; confirm with africaclimatecollaborative@cambridge-africa.cam.ac.uk. A Cali-based researcher cannot be the African applicant but could contribute as an unfunded collaborator. Salaries and overheads not covered.
opportunities.lead_applicant_requirements: Cambridge-based applicant acts as lead for administrative purposes; must register first and invite the Africa-based applicant. Both applicants post-doctoral level or above (equivalent experience considered).
opportunities.geographic_restrictions: Research must be relevant to climate resilience and sustainability on the African continent; equipment must remain with the African institution.
opportunities.consortium_details: Mandatory Cambridge + African institution pair; true collaboration must be demonstrated (not service provision). Research Project Grants require evidence of a prior successful collaboration and an internship for a graduating scholar.
opportunities.eligible_activities: Seed/catalyst research, larger collaborative research projects, skills workshops in Africa; equipment for use in Africa; priority to research engaging or benefiting young Africans (<35).
opportunities.required_documents: Case for support; itemised budget (template); lay summary; letters of support from both departments/institutions; 2-page CVs for both applicants; two suggested referees.
opportunities.application_procedure: Online savable joint application form on the Cambridge-Africa website, started by the Cambridge applicant who invites the African applicant.
opportunities.scientific_alignment_rationale: Climate resilience 'interpreted broadly' accommodates EO/AI-based crop monitoring, yield forecasting and climate-smart agriculture in Africa; small grant sizes favour seed work.
opportunities.strategic_relevance_rationale: Builds a Cambridge partnership and Africa capacity-building; small amounts and no salary/overhead coverage limit value to the Alliance.
opportunities.technical_feasibility_rationale: Seed/workshop formats (e.g., GEE/remote-sensing training workshop for young African researchers) are easily deliverable with existing skills.
opportunities.recommendation: Pursue only if an Africa-based Alliance colleague and a Cambridge counterpart (e.g., Geography, Plant Sciences, Cambridge Zero) can be lined up quickly; first confirm Alliance eligibility as the African institution. A Workshop Grant on EO/AI for crop monitoring for young African researchers is a natural fit.
opportunities.potential_partners: University of Cambridge (Dept. of Geography, Plant Sciences, Computer Science / AI for Environmental Risks), Alliance Africa hub (Nairobi), Makerere University, University of Ghana, University of Cape Town
opportunities.next_action: Email africaclimatecollaborative@cambridge-africa.cam.ac.uk to confirm whether an Alliance (CGIAR) Africa office qualifies as the African institution; identify a Cambridge lead before December 2026.

evidence.deadline_quote: The deadline for submission is 15th January 2027and applications can be submitted at any time before this.
evidence.eligibility_quote: applicants from the University of Cambridge co-create a joint project with applicants from universities (or research institutions of comparable standing to a university) on the African continent.
evidence.status_quote: We are now pleased to announce that the third round of applications is open.

opportunities.verification_notes: Loaded official Cambridge-Africa page and Guidance for Applicants 2026-27 PDF on 2026-10-14. Guidance says applications open 15 Oct 2026; the web page already states round 3 is open. CGIAR/international-organisation eligibility as African partner not addressed.

opportunities.title: Rice Methane Innovation Accelerator (Global Methane Hub)
opportunities.funder: Global Methane Hub (with Gates Foundation, Philanthropy Asia Alliance, Quadrature Climate Foundation, Temasek Life Sciences Laboratory)
opportunities.deadline_text: Not specified (no open call published). Strategy 'expected to be released in early 2026'.
opportunities.funding_text: Hub committed USD 30 million; accelerator aims to raise at least USD 100 million in philanthropic, public and private funding. Per-project amounts not specified.
opportunities.cgiar_eligibility_notes: The official announcement names IRRI, AfricaRice and the Alliance of Bioversity International and CIAT among research-ecosystem partners, so engagement is likely via direct partnership/invitation rather than an open call. Research areas include 'emissions measurement' - the entry point for rice remote sensing (AWD/flooding detection with Sentinel-1, MRV).
opportunities.eligible_activities: Four research areas: plant genetics and physiology, soil microbiome, agronomy, and emissions measurement.
opportunities.application_procedure: Not specified - no open call on official site as of 2026-10-14.
opportunities.scientific_alignment_rationale: Rice methane emissions measurement/MRV directly matches the researcher's MPhil work on satellite rice phenology and SAR/optical rice mapping.
opportunities.strategic_relevance_rationale: Alliance explicitly named as partner; large multi-funder pool; LAC/Asia/Africa rice systems.
opportunities.technical_feasibility_rationale: Existing Sentinel-1/2 rice mapping and phenology skills; would need partners for flux/chamber measurements.
opportunities.recommendation: High priority to engage proactively: contact the Alliance's existing GMH focal points and the Hub's agriculture team to position an EO-based rice methane MRV/water-management detection component in the accelerator portfolio.
opportunities.potential_partners: IRRI, AfricaRice, FLAR (Latin American Fund for Irrigated Rice), Global Research Alliance on Agricultural GHG, national rice institutes (e.g., Fedearroz Colombia)
opportunities.next_action: Ask Alliance leadership/Climate Action lever who manages the GMH relationship; request the accelerator strategy document and any planned funding windows.

evidence.eligibility_quote: Existing partners include IRRI, AfricaRice, the Alliance of Bioversity International and CIAT, national agricultural research institutes, and universities (paraphrase of official page partner list).
evidence.status_quote: Accelerator strategy ... 'expected to be released in early 2026' (no open call or application process mentioned).

opportunities.verification_notes: Loaded official GMH announcement (dated 2025-11-06) and homepage on 2026-10-14; no RFP/open call found on site. Secondary press (AgNavigator) says allocations follow a scientific committee's recommendations and funder decisions - not confirmed on official page.

opportunities.title: Gates Foundation + Google.org USD 100M for scaling AI-powered climate and crop insights to smallholders
opportunities.program: AI for smallholder farmers (Sub-Saharan Africa and South Asia)
opportunities.deadline_text: Not specified - no application route published.
opportunities.funding_text: 'direct $100 million to organizations that scale AI-powered climate and crop insights to 200 million smallholder farmers across Sub-Saharan Africa and South Asia' plus technical support from Google researchers.
opportunities.eligible_applicants: Not specified (appears directed to organizations already scaling such tools)
opportunities.eligible_countries: Sub-Saharan Africa and South Asia (implementation focus)
opportunities.cgiar_eligibility_notes: Gates' funding is mostly proactive ('majority of our funding is proactive ... independently identified by our staff'); CGIAR centers are frequent Gates grantees, so engagement would be via Gates program officers / CGIAR digital initiatives, not an open call. LAC is outside the stated geography.
opportunities.eligible_activities: Scaling real-time climate, agricultural and language AI tools/advisories for smallholders.
opportunities.scientific_alignment_rationale: Digital advisory, AI climate and crop insights, yield forecasting are core interests.
opportunities.strategic_relevance_rationale: Very large; aligns with CGIAR digital/advisory agenda in Africa; excludes LAC.
opportunities.technical_feasibility_rationale: Crop modelling/EO advisory capability exists; Africa delivery would need Alliance Africa teams.
opportunities.recommendation: Not an open call; route interest through Alliance/CGIAR Gates relationship managers and Africa digital-ag teams.
opportunities.potential_partners: Alliance Africa digital ag teams, IFPRI, Digital Green, Google Research (AgriML/weather)
opportunities.next_action: Ask Alliance partnerships office whether Gates/Google plan an RFP or direct solicitations under this commitment.

evidence.eligibility_quote: Gates: 'The majority of our funding is proactive and made to U.S. tax-exempt organizations that are independently identified by our staff.'
evidence.status_quote: Google blog (2026-09-22) gives no open call, application link, deadline or eligibility.

opportunities.verification_notes: Loaded official Google blog post on 2026-10-14. Gates press release itself not loaded. Gates 'what we do not fund' quote via search snippet of official page.

opportunities.title: Wellcome Climate Impacts Awards (annual; 2026 round closed, next round not yet announced)
opportunities.program: Climate and Health - Climate Impacts Awards
opportunities.deadline_text: 2026 round: '15:00 BST on 8 April 2026' (closed). Next round date not stated.
opportunities.funding_text: Up to GBP 2.5 million per award, up to 3 years; around 10-15 awards expected (2026 round).
opportunities.eligible_applicants: Not-for-profit administering organisations (HEIs, research institutes, NGOs) anywhere except mainland China; lead applicant mid-career or established researcher; transdisciplinary teams (lead + up to 7 co-applicants).
opportunities.cgiar_eligibility_notes: Multilateral organisations can apply but must 'contact us' first. As a not-for-profit research institute the Alliance would likely qualify as administering organisation; confirm with Wellcome.
opportunities.lead_applicant_requirements: Mid-career or established researcher with suitable long-term contract.
opportunities.consortium_details: Lead + up to seven co-applicants forming a transdisciplinary team.
opportunities.eligible_activities: Research making the health effects of climate change visible, combining health and economic arguments for policy.
opportunities.application_procedure: Via Wellcome Funding platform when a round opens.
opportunities.scientific_alignment_rationale: Health is the core outcome; EO/crop modelling would be secondary (e.g., climate-driven crop/nutrition impacts on health).
opportunities.strategic_relevance_rationale: Large awards; could link with Alliance nutrition/food-systems work.
opportunities.technical_feasibility_rationale: Requires health/epidemiology partners to lead the health evidence.
opportunities.recommendation: Monitor for the 2027 round (scope 'may not be the same next year'); only pursue with a health-research partner.
opportunities.potential_partners: LSHTM, national public health institutes in LAC/Africa, Alliance food environment/nutrition team
opportunities.next_action: Watch Wellcome Climate and Health funding listing from Dec 2026-Jan 2027.

evidence.eligibility_quote: Commercial organisations are not eligible to apply as administering organisation for this call.
evidence.status_quote: Scheme is annual; scope 'may not be the same next year'.

opportunities.verification_notes: Loaded official Wellcome scheme page 2026-10-14 (first 100k chars).
